Hi,

No, although that has been mentioned. Most of the time, it is usually enough to manipulate the lp__ symbol for Stan <= 1.3.0; the syntax is changing for stan >= 2.0.

2)  How long do you estimate that it'll take to implement sampling of discrete parameters?  The thing is that I'm writing some model excercises for newcomers to Bayesian and I want to keep the models simple.
3)  What is the difference between function abs() and fabs(). In the manual its described the same. But my model was returning wierd outputs till I've added the "f" in front of all abs.

This may have been harmonized for the next version of Stan. fabs() is for floating-point numbers.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: few question
parts:
On 8/8/13 10:59 AM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> On Thursday, August 8, 2013 10:48:39 AM UTC-4, Martin Šmíra wrote:
>
> 1) I'm trying to find out if Stan has an alternative tool to WinBugs WBDev, where I could define my own function
> and then just call it in a model specification?
>
>
> No, although that has been mentioned. Most of the time, it is usually enough to manipulate the lp__ symbol for Stan <=
> 1.3.0; the syntax is changing for stan >= 2.0.

Basically, what used to be written as:

lp__ <- lp__ + y;

will be written as:

increment_log_prob(y);

The reason was to cut down on user errors for forgetting
to increment. You can use this to implement just about any density,
though Stan's lack of good debugging and compiler tools makes it
a challenge to implement anything too difficult (HMMs and Gaussian
processes are about as far as I've gone within Stan).

You can also pretty easily link in templated C++ definitions,
though there's not an easy extension mechanism besides rebuilding
Stan at the moment. We will be adding that soon so that you can
dynamically link in new functions defined externally to Stan's own
code.

> 2) How long do you estimate that it'll take to implement sampling of discrete parameters? The thing is that I'm
> writing some model excercises for newcomers to Bayesian and I want to keep the models simple.
>
>
> poisson(1000)

Unit free estimates, to boot :-)

We're thinking about discrete sampling, but don't have a concrete
plan or time frame yet. And unless we have some conceptual breakthroughs,
it will likely be a bit clunky and redundant even when we do add it.

> 3) What is the difference between function abs() and fabs(). In the manual its described the same. But my model was
> returning wierd outputs till I've added the "f" in front of all abs.
>
>
> This may have been harmonized for the next version of Stan. fabs() is for floating-point numbers.

It's all about the signatures, and particularly the return types:

int abs(int);

and

real fabs(real);


Because int can be promoted to real, the second can also be used as:

real fabs(int);

So the f vs. no-f controls the type of the result.

You see the same thing with fmax and max, where there's further subtlety
due to multiple arguments.

- Bob
